patch.description: SiC power MOSFETs (600-1,200 V class) redesigned to run near rated voltage in space, whether by empirical hardening or with a mechanism-level model of heavy-ion single-event burnout and leakage degradation. Achieved when a vendor qualifies such a part free of single-event burnout at 80% or more of rated voltage under standard heavy-ion testing (the signpost).
patch.why: Not an AI-math implication: vendors are already hardening SiC empirically with TCAD and beam tests (CoolCAD's vendor-reported burnout threshold above 900 V at LET above 40, Jul 2026), so the date is set by fab cycles and heavy-ion beam time, and the P7 Speculative default does not apply. High-voltage (300-800 V class) buses cut harness mass and losses for 100 kW-class orbital compute and electric propulsion; derating 1,200 V parts to ~50% throws away much of SiC's advantage. LEO plasma arcing on high-voltage arrays also limits bus voltage (NASA-HDBK-4006, general). Explaining the burnout mechanism (impact ionization and thermal runaway along the ion track, defect physics) is a physics-theory problem that AI could speed (cap-physics-theory, P6, soft), but theory is an accelerator, not a prerequisite; each redesign takes about a year per fab cycle plus beam tests, which bind. Chain (S2): hardened-by-design parts reported 2026 -> one or two redesign, fab and beam-test cycles 2027-29 -> a part qualified free of burnout at 80% or more of rated voltage 2030. Band Medium in S2 and S3 (judgment): the empirical route is close but the mechanism is still debated and the rad-hard power market is small, so fab priority is low. S3 2029 through faster design iteration; S1 2031 and Low because a capability plateau slows design iteration and the soft theory input arrives late.
